tasks.source: the Port of Barcelona's 2024 container calls at quays 24B (APM Terminals Barcelona) and 36A (Terminal Catalunya, BEST), as PortSimEnv's dock-v1-eval one-week standard and busy weeks, with the port's 2024 pilot and tug traffic; the wind that blew at Meteocat's XEMA station Y7 and the ECMWF open-data forecasts as issued, in real Barcelona weather weeks of 2023 to 2025; each ship's agent is the firm the 2024 record names for the call
tasks.selection: the 15 wind weeks, all qualifying: (a) at least 3 of the follower's 4 configurations finish feasible, (b) the silent follower, which never asks the ships' agents, scores at most 0.9 in at least 3 of 4, so asking matters, and (c) the week has at most 10 watches

grading.reference: min(the hindsight optimum, which knows every arrival and asks each ship at the first watch its agent could commit, the best cost of the follower re-planner, which asks the ships' agents, over its 4 solver configurations)
grading.reward: a feasible week scores 0.2 + 0.8 exp(-g/0.5), g = max(0, cost - reference) / (max(0, reference - floor) + 100), the floor being the cost no plan can avoid; a week that breaks a rule scores 0.2 times its share of clean ships, below 0.2, and a ship left without a window breaks a rule; graded once, on the windows confirmed and the week as it really happened
grading.excused: cost or rule breaks that news, or wind the forecast didn't show at that ship's last chance, brings to a window after its last chance to change, per ship; wind the forecast showed then is charged; an ETA that proves wrong is not news: a late ship's lateness and an early one's hours at anchor are charged, and a ship whose arrival was agreed arrives at that hour

baselines.name: follower re-planner, asking the ships' agents
